newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila defends, leftists slam APEC preparations.
newsitem.headline: Manila defends, leftists slam APEC preparations.

text.p: Leftist groups on Wednesday accused Manila of going overboard in preparations for the summit of the APEC forum, but President Fidel Ramos said the Philippines must put on its best face as host.
Leaders of leftist organisations planning to hold an anti-APEC meeting to coincide with the November 25 summit accused police of harassing their supporters and putting them under surveillance.
Thousands of squatters around Manila have been driven out of their shanties and their huts demolished to hide widespread poverty, leftist leader Satur Ocampo told a news conference.

"The regime has gone overboard in its overweening desire to create (the impression) that the Philippines has turned from 'a sick of man of Asia' into an economic 'tiger cub' as a come-on to foreign investments," Ocampo said.

A spokeswoman for a peasants' group said that as part of security preparations, soldiers were preventing farmers from harvesting crops planted in areas near the summit site in Subic Bay, northeast of Manila.
A military spokesman denied the accusations.

Leftist groups are to hold a "People's Conference against Imperialist Globalisation" on November 21-23 in parallel with the summit of the 18 member economies of APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation).

The leftist conference, aimed at showing that the APEC goal of trade liberalisation would only widen the gap between its rich and less advanced members, is to be attended by activists from the Asian region, Ocampo said.

Ramos, inaugurating a Manila road widening project, made no reference to the leftists' allegations but asked Filipinos to bear the temporary inconveniences, such as traffic jams, caused by the road improvements.
"There is no gain without pain," he said. "We undertook their improvement...as part of our efforts to put on our best face with the holding of the summit," he said.
"These efforts are natural and understandable on our part, as host to the country's biggest event in this decade."
